title: Signed FlyWire wiring from photoreceptors predicted the measured ON or OFF sign of 14 of 18 fly visual cell types only when glutamate was inhibitory; most errors were in weakly driven types
abstract: We tested a parameter-free sign rule in the Drosophila optic lobe. Photoreceptors are ON. Each cell type gets the sign of its summed input, weighted by synapse fraction in the FlyWire v783 type graph, with acetylcholine excitatory and GABA, glutamate and histamine inhibitory. We compared the predicted sign with the ON or OFF sign that we measured from the phase of 0.1 Hz full-field flicker calcium responses (Currier and Clandinin 2025, 60 flies, 89 types). In 18 types with a clear measured sign and a FlyWire name, the right optic lobe predicted 14 correct signs and the left 13. Transmitter-label permutation gave mean accuracy 0.46 and one-sided p = 0.051 (right) and 0.092 (left). Predicted drive and measured polarity strength had Spearman rho 0.64 and 0.61 (p < 0.01). If glutamate was excitatory, only 7 of 18 signs were correct; a GABA sign change had no effect; without photoreceptor histamine nearly all signs inverted. Types with the strongest predicted drive had 82% correct signs, the weakest third 36 to 55%. In 29 types with at least 3 flies, accuracy was 0.72 and 0.66. Limitations: small sample, moderate p values, full-field calcium measurements, different flies for anatomy and activity, uncertain name matches, a linear steady-state model, and a primary setting fixed after a short trial run.
